The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights in Al-Adsani v. United Kingdom (2001) held that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait in a torture damages claim did not violate the applicant's right of access to a court under Article 6(1), finding that state immunity remained a legitimate restriction and that no torture exception had yet crystallized in international law. The application was therefore dismissed. However, the Court did not treat sovereign immunity as automatically overriding Convention guarantees whenever they clashed; it applied a proportionality-style analysis and left open whether such an exception might develop.
CONFIDENCE: 95
